candidates.change_summary: Change block offset from +1 to +0 so settle uses the current block hash instead of the next block's hash.
Change block offset from +1 to +2 so settle uses a different future block hash.
Delete the line that sets guesses[msg.sender].block so it remains zero, preventing settle from ever proceeding.
Delete the guess assignment so the stored guess remains bytes32(0), changing the condition checked in settle.
Delete the require(msg.value == 1 ether) check so lockInGuess can be called with zero payment, altering contract balance and possible payouts.
Change require value from 1 ether to 0 ether so users can lock in without payment.
Change require value from 1 ether to 2 ether so lockInGuess requires more funds.
Insert an additional assignment that adds 1 to block number, making the stored block off by one.
Remove the requirement that the sender has not already locked in a guess, allowing repeated calls to overwrite the stored guess and block number.
Change the required payment from 1 ether to 0 ether, allowing calls with no value.
Change the required payment from 1 ether to 2 ether, requiring a different call value.
Change the payment guard from equality to a minimum, allowing any value of at least 1 ether.
Store the current block number instead of the next block number, shifting the settlement target block.
Store block number plus two instead of plus one, shifting the settlement target block.
Store the supplied hash as the block marker instead of the actual block number, corrupting the stored guess state.
Overwrite the caller's stored guess before the state checks, so a failed call still changes the stored guess.
Remove the assignment that records the caller's locked-in guess hash, so guesses[msg.sender].guess remains zero after lockInGuess completes.
Replace the recorded guess hash with the zero value, so guesses[msg.sender].guess becomes 0x00...00 instead of the supplied hash.
Record the guess in guesses[msg.sender].block instead of guesses[msg.sender].guess, leaving the guess hash unset and putting the hash value into the block field.
Set the lock block to the current block number instead of the next block number, so the recorded block differs from the original lock-in value.
Change the lock condition from requiring the stored block to be zero to requiring the stored block to be nonzero.
Change the lock condition from checking the caller's stored block to checking the caller's zero address.
Change the required payment from exactly 1 ether to exactly 2 ether.
Change the required payment condition from equality with 1 ether to an inequality.
Remove the payment requirement so callers no longer need to send exactly 1 ether.
Store the supplied hash in the block field instead of the guess field.
Store the block number in the guess field instead of the supplied hash.
Set the future block to the current block instead of the next block number.
Set the future block two blocks ahead instead of one block ahead.
Insert an extra assignment that zeroes the stored block just before storing the new block number.
Move the block assignment before the guess assignment.
Delete the assignment that stores the supplied hash into the guess field.
Delete the assignment that stores the future block number.
Change the stored guess from the supplied hash to the function selector bytes of lockInGuess(bytes32).
Remove the assignment that stores the supplied hash into the caller's guess.
Change the lock block from one block after the current block to the current block itself.
Change the lock block from one block after the current block to the current block plus two.
Remove the requirement that the caller's existing guess block is zero.
Change the required payment from exactly one ether to at least one ether.
Change the required payment from exactly one ether to at most one ether.
Change the required payment to zero ether, allowing no-value calls to lock in a guess.
Remove the assignment that marks the caller as having locked in a guess by setting the block.
Store the hash into the wrong mapping field, i.e. into the caller's block field instead of the guess field.
Delete the exact one-ether payment requirement, allowing any payment amount to lock in a guess.
Insert an extra requirement that the caller has not already locked in any nonzero block.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number, making the lock-in block equal to the current block instead of the next one.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number - 1, shifting the lock-in block earlier than the current block.
Store the hash into the block field instead of the guess field, corrupting the observable Guess.block value.
Store block.number + 1 into the guess field instead of assigning the supplied hash to guess.
Remove the require that the caller has no existing nonzero block, allowing a second lockInGuess call to overwrite the stored guess and block.
Remove the require that exactly 1 ether is sent, allowing lock-in with any msg.value including zero.
Weaken the first guard to require the block field be nonzero, excluding first-time callers whose block is zero from locking in.
Insert a reset of the stored block to zero after storing the new block, so the guess never survives as locked in.
Move the block assignment before the guess assignment, so the block field is set before the supplied hash is stored.
The guess hash is stored before the block number, so the externally visible state read after lockInGuess completes has the same guess value but a different block timestamp.
The lock-in block is set to the current block number, making the recorded block differ from the original block.number + 1.
The lock-in block is set to block.number + 2, making the recorded block differ from the original block.number + 1.
The guess hash is not stored, so the externally visible guess remains zero instead of the supplied hash.
Replace the requirement that the caller's guess block is zero with a requirement that it is non-zero, changing when lockInGuess can succeed.
Replace the required msg.value equality with 1 ether with a required msg.value equality to 2 ether, changing which calls are accepted.
Replace the stored block number with block.number instead of block.number + 1, changing the value later observed by settle and the lock timing.
Replace the stored block number with block.number + 2 instead of block.number + 1, delaying the lock and changing the observed block value.
Store the hash value in the block field and the block number in the guess field, swapping the assigned values.
Delete the requirement that msg.value equals 1 ether, allowing lockInGuess to be called with any amount.
Delete the assignment to guesses[msg.sender].guess, so the guess hash is not stored.
Delete the assignment to guesses[msg.sender].block, so the lock marker is not stored.
Change the block-number assignment from block.number + 1 to block.number.
Change the block-number assignment from block.number + 1 to block.number + 2.
Remove the + 1 offset by subtracting 1 from block.number.
Remove the assignment storing the guess hash, so lockInGuess no longer records the chosen hash.
Store the caller address instead of the supplied hash as the guess.
Store the block hash of the current block instead of the supplied hash.
Require exactly 2 ether instead of 1 ether in lockInGuess.
Change the payment requirement to reject exactly 1 ether by requiring msg.value != 1 ether.
Remove the 1 ether payment requirement from lockInGuess.
Invert the uninitialized-guess guard to require that the block is nonzero.
Remove the guard preventing a second guess from overwriting an existing one.
Move the uninitialized-guess guard so it runs after storing the new guess hash.
Move the payment check so it runs after the guess state has been updated.
Remove the require that checks the guesser has sent 1 ether, allowing zero-value settlements to still transfer 2 ether.
Change the transfer amount from 2 ether to 1 ether, altering the balance change observable after a successful settle.
Remove the balance check so that settle can succeed even if the contract has less than 2 ether, then transfer nonetheless.
Change the answer computation to use a different block number (block.number) so that a correct guess never matches.
Change the payout from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Change the balance requirement from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Change the block-number check from strictly greater than to greater than or equal to.
Change the guess equality check to an inequality check.
Remove the condition wrapping the payout so it always transfers when settle succeeds.
Replace the require that the guess block is nonzero with a require that it is zero.
Delete the block-number maturity check.
Delete the requirement that the guess block be nonzero.
Delete the balance requirement before payout.
Delete the payout transfer while leaving the balance requirement.
Change the guard from requiring block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block to requiring block.number >= guesses[msg.sender].block, allowing settlement in the same block.
Change the reset assignment to set guesses[msg.sender].block to 1 instead of 0.
Change the answer hash to use block.number instead of the stored guess block.
Remove the final hash wrapper and directly compare the raw blockhash to the stored guess.
Change the winning payout transfer amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Change the balance guard from requiring at least 2 ether to requiring at least 1 ether.
Delete the requirement that the stored guess block is nonzero.
Delete the requirement that the current block number is greater than the stored guess block.
Delete the reset of the stored guess block to zero before payout.
Delete the balance requirement before the winning transfer.
Change the equality check in the payout condition to an inequality check.
Changed the settle payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Changed the settle comparison to always be true, so a correct or incorrect guess always triggers the payout when funded.
Changed the settle comparison to always be false, so the payout is never made.
Changed the answer hash to be computed from the post-settlement reset block number rather than the guessed block number.
Changed the eligibility check to require that the current block is at least one greater than the stored block, instead of strictly greater.
Remove the balance check before transferring 2 ether to the caller.
Change the settlement payout from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Require the contract balance to be at least 1 ether instead of 2 ether before paying out.
Use the current block hash in the answer calculation instead of the guessed future block hash.
Remove the resetting of the caller's guess block before payout.
Change the timing requirement to block.number < guesses[msg.sender].block instead of greater than.
Change the settlement payout requirement from at least 2 ether to at least 3 ether, making a successful settle revert or no-op when the contract holds exactly 2 ether.
Change the settlement payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether, altering the amount transferred to a successful guesser.
Change the lock-time check from strictly greater than the recorded block to strictly less than it, making settle callable only before the target block instead of after.
Change the guess equality check to an inequality check, so the contract pays out exactly when the guess is wrong rather than correct.
Replace the answer derivation with the current block hash instead of the stored guess block hash, changing which settlement attempts succeed.
Reset the stored guess hash to zero instead of the stored block number, corrupting the recorded guess so later settle calls compare against zero.
Delete the reset of the stored block number to zero, leaving a settled guess active so it can be settled again if conditions allow.
Replace the direct ether transfer with a self-payout to the contract address, so a successful settlement pays the contract instead of the caller.
Replace the strict block-number check with a non-strict one, allowing settlement in the same block as the locked-in guess.
Remove the requirement that the caller has an active guess, allowing calls from addresses that never locked in a guess.
Remove the requirement that the current block is after the guessed block, allowing settlement too early.
Change the answer computation to use the current block hash instead of the guessed block hash.
Change the answer computation to hash the raw guessed block number instead of its block hash.
Change the answer computation to hash the caller's address instead of the guessed block hash.
Change the answer computation to hash the constant zero instead of the guessed block hash.
Reset the stored block to 1 instead of 0 after settlement, preventing future lock-ins.
Delete the statement that resets the stored guess block to zero after settlement.
Invert the equality check so that the payout occurs when the guess is wrong.
Lower the payout requirement from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Increase the payout amount from 2 ether to 3 ether.
Delete the balance requirement, allowing the transfer to be attempted regardless of contract balance.
Delete the entire payout branch, so a correct guess never transfers ether.
Move the reset of the stored guess block to before the answer computation.
Change the block-number comparison from > to >=, allowing settlement one block earlier.
Change the reset of the caller's guess block from 0 to 1, preventing lockInGuess after settlement from passing its block == 0 check.
Change the payout transfer from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Change the answer hash to include the caller's address, altering which guesses match.
Delete the balance check before payout, allowing a reverting transfer when the contract has less than 2 ether.
Delete the require that a guess block is set, allowing settle on accounts with no guess.
Change the payout recipient from msg.sender to address(this).
Change the answer to a constant hash, altering the matching condition.
Change the answer to use the current block hash instead of the guess block hash.
Change the balance requirement from at least 2 ether to at least 1 ether while paying 2 ether.
Change the balance requirement from at least 2 ether to strictly greater than 2 ether.
Change the guess equality check to inequality, paying out when the guess is wrong.
Change the reset of the caller's guess block from zeroing the block number to only zeroing the guess value.
Move the reset of the caller's guess block to before the answer computation.
Move the balance check to before the guess reset, still inside the winning branch.
Change the settle balance check from requiring at least 2 ether to requiring at least 1 ether.
Change the settle payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Change the settle block-number timing check from strictly greater than to greater than or equal to.
Change the answered-guess comparison from equality to inequality.
